body:
Electronic payments and the banking system

A digital payment transfers value through an electronic payment arrangement rather than by handing over physical currency. In India, participating banks, payment-system operators and applications perform different functions in completing these transactions.

Money held in a bank account is different from the application used to instruct a payment. A payment application supplies the user interface, while the banking and payment infrastructure processes the transfer. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) operates several important retail payment systems under the country's payment-system regulatory framework, with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) serving as the relevant regulator.

Unified Payments Interface

UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface. Developed by NPCI and introduced in 2016, it enables instant electronic payments between participating accounts. It supports payments using identifiers such as a UPI ID and payment requests initiated through participating applications.

For a typical bank-account-based UPI payment, the user registers through a participating application, links an eligible bank account using the required verification process and authorises outgoing transactions using a UPI PIN. The application is the interface; UPI is the underlying interoperable payment system.

For example, a person using a UPI application can pay a merchant who displays a supported UPI QR code. The transaction uses the UPI payment system and the participating financial institutions. The merchant does not need to use the same consumer-facing application as the payer, provided the systems support the transaction.

BHIM: An application that uses UPI

BHIM stands for Bharat Interface for Money. It is an NPCI-developed payment application launched on 30 December 2016. BHIM enables users to initiate UPI payments.

BHIM and UPI are not synonyms. BHIM is one application using UPI. Other supported banking and payment applications can also use the UPI infrastructure. Therefore, a question asking for the payment system should be answered differently from a question asking for the name of a particular application.

RuPay: A card payment network

RuPay is India's card payment network, developed and operated by NPCI. Participating financial institutions issue RuPay debit, credit and prepaid cards. The network supports card transactions through the applicable acceptance channels.

A RuPay card is not the same as a UPI application. However, supported RuPay credit cards can be linked to UPI for permitted merchant payments, subject to the applicable bank, card and service conditions. This connection between systems does not erase the distinction between the RuPay card network and UPI.

Aadhaar Enabled Payment System

AePS stands for Aadhaar Enabled Payment System. It is a bank-led arrangement developed by NPCI that enables specified financial transactions at authorised banking touchpoints, such as a business correspondent's micro-ATM, using Aadhaar authentication.

A customer generally needs an Aadhaar-enabled bank account, the relevant bank identification and successful authentication through the permitted procedure. Supported services can include cash withdrawal, balance enquiry and other banking functions according to the system's available services.

AePS differs from an ordinary UPI application payment. AePS uses Aadhaar-based authentication at an authorised banking touchpoint; a standard bank-account-based UPI transaction commonly uses an application and UPI PIN.

Compare the payment systems

SystemCategoryResponsible organisationTypical use
UPIInteroperable payment systemNPCIInstant electronic account payments
BHIMPayment applicationNPCI BHIM Services Limited, a wholly owned NPCI subsidiaryInitiating UPI transactions
RuPayCard payment networkNPCITransactions using participating cards
AePSAadhaar-enabled banking systemNPCI and participating banksBanking transactions through authorised touchpoints

Direct Benefit Transfer and PFMS

Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) refers to the transfer of eligible government benefits or subsidies through the relevant government payment arrangements, commonly into beneficiaries' bank accounts. It is a method of benefit delivery, not a general shopping-payment application.

PFMS, the Public Financial Management System, is a government financial-management and payment platform developed through the Controller General of Accounts, Ministry of Finance. It supports government financial processes, including payments and reporting connected with DBT.

The government scheme determines who is eligible and what benefit is payable. The financial system executes the authorised payment. An Aadhaar number, a UPI ID or a PFMS record does not independently establish entitlement to the scheme.

Status at the 14 November 2026 cutoff: UPI, BHIM, RuPay, AePS and PFMS were operating digital payment or financial-management arrangements. They should be classified by function rather than treated as 5 separate welfare schemes.

Prelims focus

  • UPI: Unified Payments Interface, developed by NPCI and introduced in 2016.
  • BHIM: Bharat Interface for Money, launched on 30 December 2016.
  • RuPay: card payment network operated by NPCI.
  • AePS: Aadhaar Enabled Payment System, using Aadhaar authentication for specified banking transactions.
  • PFMS: government financial-management system associated with the Controller General of Accounts.
  • Trap: BHIM is an application; UPI is the underlying payment system.

[NPCI, 'UPI: Frequently Asked Questions', definition, account linking and UPI PIN; NPCI, 'Milestones', UPI introduction and payment-system development; NPCI, BHIM press release, 2017, launch on 30 December 2016; NPCI, 'RuPay Card Variants' and 'Credit Card on UPI', payment-network functions; NPCI, 'Product Booklet: Aadhaar Enabled Payment System', November 2025, transaction types and eligibility; Government of India, Department of Expenditure, 'Mandatory Use of PFMS for Payment, Accounting and Reporting under DBT', 23 December 2014; NCERT, Understanding Economic Development, Class 10, Chapter 3, 'Money and Credit', printed pp. 39–41; official online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]

title: Digital Payments: UPI, BHIM, RuPay, AePS and Benefit Transfers

body:
Gujarat's digital service-delivery system

Gujarat operates several state-level digital service facilities. These are not interchangeable. Some provide access to general government services, some support village-level assisted delivery, and others specialise in land records, revenue applications or urban services.

For objective examinations, the most reliable way to distinguish them is to identify the responsible authority, the service offered and the intended user or service area.

Digital Gujarat Portal

The Digital Gujarat Portal is a common online service portal of the Government of Gujarat. It provides a single point of access to participating state government services, including applications for specified certificates and other citizen services.

The portal was conceptualised by Gujarat Informatics Limited (GIL) and developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC) in consultation with Gujarat's Science and Technology Department.

Citizens can use the portal or supported service channels to submit applications, upload required documents, make applicable payments and track requests. For example, a student may use an available scholarship-related service, but eligibility for any scholarship is determined by the rules of the scholarship concerned. Access to the portal does not itself award financial assistance.

Digital Seva Setu and e-Gram

Digital Seva Setu is a Gujarat government initiative for delivering government services at the village level. It was launched on 8 October 2020. The responsible state departments identified by Gujarat Informatics Limited are the Science and Technology Department and the General Administration Department.

Digital Seva Setu uses the e-Gram service-centre network to make participating government services available closer to rural residents. Instead of travelling to a taluka or district office for every application, a resident can approach a participating village service centre.

The distinction is important: e-Gram is the village-level service access network, while Digital Seva Setu is a service-delivery initiative operating through that network. DigiLocker may be used within the broader service process for access to eligible electronic documents, but it is a separate national document platform.

AnyRoR and i-ORA: Land records and revenue applications

The Revenue Department, Government of Gujarat, provides specialised online services for land and revenue administration.

  • AnyRoR: provides online viewing of Record of Rights (RoR) information, particularly rural land records such as the commonly used 7/12 record.
  • i-ORA: provides facilities for submitting specified online revenue applications, including applications concerning land and revenue permissions or records.

The key difference is between viewing a land record and applying for a revenue-related action. A record available for viewing does not mean that the portal independently approves a change in ownership, permission or revenue classification. Such actions remain subject to the competent revenue authority and the applicable procedure.

eNagar 2.0: Urban local government services

eNagar 2.0 is a Gujarat government platform for delivering services through Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), including municipalities and municipal corporations. The relevant state department is the Urban Development and Urban Housing Department, with the Gujarat Urban Development Mission (GUDM) serving as the nodal organisation for the eNagar project.

Its services include property tax, water and drainage services, marriage registration, shops and establishments, complaints and grievances, and other participating municipal functions.

For example, a resident of an urban area may use eNagar 2.0 to pay municipal property tax. This is different from using AnyRoR to view a rural land record or using Digital Seva Setu to obtain an assisted village-level service.

Gujarat Single Sign-On

Gujarat Citizen Single Sign-On (Gujarat SSO or GOG eSuvidha) is a state initiative under the Science and Technology Department that provides a common authentication and login mechanism for participating government services.

Single Sign-On means that a user can use one recognised login arrangement to access multiple linked services instead of maintaining a completely separate login for each. An SSO system identifies or authenticates the user; it does not automatically replace the government department that issues a certificate, maintains a land record or approves a service.

Compare Gujarat's service platforms

Platform or initiativeResponsible authorityPrincipal purpose
Digital GujaratGovernment of Gujarat; GIL and NICCommon access to state government e-services
Digital Seva SetuScience and Technology Department and General Administration DepartmentVillage-level government service delivery
e-GramGovernment of Gujarat's village service-centre networkAssisted access to digital services in villages
AnyRoRRevenue DepartmentOnline viewing of rural land records
i-ORARevenue DepartmentOnline revenue-related applications
eNagar 2.0Urban Development and Urban Housing Department; GUDMMunicipal and urban services
Gujarat SSOScience and Technology DepartmentCommon login for participating state services

These initiatives were described as operating service facilities on their respective official state government websites at the 14 November 2026 content cutoff. Actual availability, documentary requirements and eligibility may differ among the individual services.

Complete revision of the national and Gujarat initiatives

The following distinctions connect the entire subtopic:

  • Internet infrastructure: BharatNet develops rural broadband infrastructure.
  • Public internet access: PM-WANI enables participating local public Wi-Fi hotspots.
  • Digital skills: PMGDISHA trained eligible rural people and concluded on 31 March 2024.
  • Language access: BHASHINI provides AI-based translation and speech technologies.
  • Identity: Aadhaar is issued through UIDAI and supports identification and authentication.
  • Documents: DigiLocker provides access to authentic digital documents.
  • Government services: UMANG and Digital Gujarat provide interfaces for participating services at their respective levels.
  • Digital payments: UPI is the payment system, BHIM is an application, RuPay is a card network and AePS is an Aadhaar-enabled banking system.
  • Specialised Gujarat services: AnyRoR concerns land-record viewing, i-ORA concerns revenue applications, and eNagar 2.0 concerns urban local government services.

Prelims focus

  • Digital Seva Setu: launched on 8 October 2020; village services through e-Gram.
  • Digital Gujarat: common service portal associated with GIL and NIC.
  • AnyRoR: rural Record of Rights; i-ORA: revenue applications.
  • eNagar 2.0: services of municipalities and municipal corporations.
  • Gujarat SSO: common authentication and login system.
  • Trap: A portal providing access to an application does not itself establish eligibility or guarantee approval.

[Gujarat Informatics Limited, 'Digital Gujarat Portal (Common Service Portal)', project description and key features; Gujarat Informatics Limited, 'Digital Seva Setu', objective, departments and launch date; Gujarat Informatics Limited, 'e-Gram', service delivery; Gujarat Informatics Limited, 'Gujarat Citizen Single Sign On (GOG eSuvidha)', project description; Revenue Department, Government of Gujarat, 'Online Services' and 'iORA Service', service categories; Gujarat Urban Development Mission, 'eNagar 2.0: About Us' and 'Online Services', urban service categories; official state government websites consulted 14 November 2026.]
